The Superiority of the Chosen People

precepts.text: He took his brother by the heel in the womb and by his strength he had power with God, yea, he had power over the angel and prevailed; his name was changed because of his strength.
precepts.point: Jacob was trained by Isaac and Abraham; imagine his descendants, David running through warriors, Samson; our forefathers were intellectual and physically powerful, and Jacob was a god on the earth.

note.label: The Superiority of the Chosen People

precepts.why:
“And Jacob was left alone; and there wrestled a man with him until the breaking of the day.” He fought for hours. In a real fight you are exhausted long before daybreak; a boxing match is twelve rounds, and Jacob fought until the break of day. “when he saw that he prevailed not against him, he touched the hollow of his thigh;” and put it out of joint. The angel had to dislocate Jacob’s thigh to stop him. Even then Jacob held on: “I will not let thee go, except thou bless me.”

“Thy name shall be called no more Jacob, but Israel: for as a prince hast thou power with God and with men, and hast prevailed.” That is what the name means: a prince with power with God.

Hosea 12:3-4 says why his name was changed: “He took his brother by the heel in the womb, and by his strength he had power with God: Yea, he had power over the angel, and prevailed: he wept, and made supplication unto him: he found him in Beth–el, and there he spake with us.” By his strength. His name was changed to Israel because of how strong he was. This was no slap boxing; it went back and forth, and there is no other record in the Bible of any man wrestling with an angel and prevailing. Jacob was a god on the earth.

He was trained to fight. Abraham had trained servants, armed them, and went to war to bring Lot back; Isaac knew it as well, and they taught Jacob. Imagine his descendants: David running through warriors, Samson, a warlike race. Our forefathers were intellectual as well as physically powerful; Abraham knew arithmetic and taught astronomy. That is why this superiority is stressed: white people, and even some of our own who move in their circles, say we are stupid and have low IQ, and many of us believe it. The white teacher told Malcolm X, top of his class, that being a lawyer was no profession for a nigga, and he should be a carpenter. The scriptures say otherwise about the children of Israel.

precepts.text: Before the throne of the Most High the hosts of angels stand with trembling; the host Jacob saw was the angels.
precepts.point: When the scriptures speak of the Lord of hosts, the hosts are the armies of angels that stand before Him.
precepts.why:
“Whose throne is inestimable; whose glory may not be comprehended; before whom the hosts of angels stand with trembling”. The hosts that stand before the throne of the Most High are the angels. When the scriptures speak of the Lord of hosts, the hosts are the armies of angels that stand before Him.

So the host Jacob saw was the angels. As he departed from Laban, “the angels of God met him”, and he said, “This is God’s host”, and called the place Mahanaim, which means two hosts or camps.

precepts.text: Esau hated Jacob because of the blessing and said in his heart, I will slay my brother Jacob; that was the last report Jacob had.
precepts.point: The violent man imagines mischiefs in his heart and is continually gathered together for war; that is what Jacob understood was coming toward him.
precepts.why:
“And Esau hated Jacob because of the blessing wherewith his father blessed him: and Esau said in his heart, The days of mourning for my father are at hand; then will I slay my brother Jacob.” Rebekah heard of it and warned Jacob that Esau “doth comfort himself, purposing to kill thee.”

That was the last report Jacob had of his brother. So when the messengers returned saying that Esau “cometh to meet thee, and four hundred men with him”, Jacob “was greatly afraid and distressed”, and rightfully. The hatred began at the blessing, and the scriptures show in Ezekiel that the hatred never ended.

precepts.text: Deliver me from the evil man, preserve me from the violent man, which imagine mischiefs in their heart; Jacob's prayer fit the psalm.
precepts.point: The violent man imagines mischiefs in his heart and is continually gathered together for war; that is what Jacob understood was coming toward him.
precepts.why:
“Deliver me, O Lord, from the evil man: preserve me from the violent man; Which imagine mischiefs in their heart; continually are they gathered together for war.”

That is what Jacob understood was coming toward him: Esau with four hundred men, the violent man that imagines mischiefs in his heart and is continually gathered together for war. Esau had purposed in his heart to slay him, and now he came with an army. Jacob's prayer for deliverance fit the psalm.

precepts.text: A man's gift maketh room for him; the present went before Jacob to make room.
precepts.point: What he did was scriptural: a man's gift maketh room for him, and bringeth him before great men.
precepts.why:
“A man’s gift maketh room for him, and bringeth him before great men.”

That is exactly what Jacob did. He sent droves of livestock ahead as a present, spaced apart, “a space betwixt drove and drove”, with each servant instructed what to say: “it is a present sent unto my lord Esau: and, behold, also he is behind us.” He said, “I will appease him with the present that goeth before me, and afterward I will see his face; peradventure he will accept of me.” He moved strategically to soften Esau before they met face to face, and what he did was scriptural: the gift went before him to make room for him.

precepts.text: Cleave unto Him and depart not away, that thou mayest be increased at thy last end; hold on until the blessing.
precepts.point: That is the spirit to carry through hardship: fight the good fight of faith and lay hold on eternal life the way Jacob laid hold and would not let go.
precepts.why:
“Cleave unto him, and depart not away, that thou mayest be increased at thy last end.”

Jacob is the picture of it. A man wrestled with him until the breaking of the day and had to put the hollow of his thigh out of joint, because Jacob would not be beaten. Even then he held on: “I will not let thee go, except thou bless me.” That is faith with works: cleaving to the Most High and not departing, thigh out of joint, until he was increased at his last end with the blessing.

precepts.text: Fight the good fight of faith; lay hold on eternal life as Jacob laid hold until he was blessed.
precepts.point: That is the spirit to carry through hardship: fight the good fight of faith and lay hold on eternal life the way Jacob laid hold and would not let go.
precepts.why:
“Fight the good fight of faith, lay hold on eternal life, whereunto thou art also called”.

Jacob laid hold and would not let go. With his thigh out of joint he still said, “I will not let thee go, except thou bless me.” That is faith with works, and it is the spirit to carry through hardship: fight the good fight of faith and lay hold on eternal life the way Jacob laid hold until he was blessed.

precepts.text: The God of Israel is He that giveth strength and power unto His people; the power of the name is from Him.
precepts.point: The God of Israel is He that giveth strength and power unto His people; He is the power source. When Israel went astray and served other gods, the name and the power were taken, and the nations called the people by every other name. Returning to the Most High is how the power returns, not carnal weapons of warfare.
precepts.why:
“O God, thou art terrible out of thy holy places: the God of Israel is he that giveth strength and power unto his people. Blessed be God.” The God of Israel is the power source; strength and power come from Him.

That is the power in the name. “Thy name shall be called no more Jacob, but Israel: for as a prince hast thou power with God and with men, and hast prevailed.” Israel means a prince that has power with God. When Israel went astray and served other gods, the name and the power were taken, and the nations called the people by every other name. Returning to the Most High is how the power returns, not carnal weapons of warfare.

precepts.text: Jacob had power with God; he had power over the angel, and prevailed; the wrestler was an angel.
precepts.point: The one Jacob wrestled was an angel: by his strength he had power with God, yea, he had power over the angel, and prevailed. The word God, Elohim, is plural, which clears up the passages where men are said to have seen God and yet no man hath seen the Father.
precepts.why:
“He took his brother by the heel in the womb, and by his strength he had power with God: Yea, he had power over the angel, and prevailed: he wept, and made supplication unto him”. Hosea tells who Jacob wrestled: he had power with God, and he had power over the angel. The wrestler was an angel.

The man would not give his name, but he blessed Jacob there, and Jacob called the place Peniel: “for I have seen God face to face, and my life is preserved.” The word God, Elohim, is plural, which clears up the passages where men are said to have seen God and yet no man hath seen the Father. Jacob saw God face to face in the angel.
